description:
FILED s464aw (found by a #972 review probe; PRE-EXISTING -- identical on an
80b715c worktree).

    package S1; use overload q("") => sub { "AB" }; sub new { bless {}, shift }
    my $a = S1->new; my $b = S1->new;
    "$a$b"     perl ABAB   PCL ABAB      <- two DISTINCT objects: fine
    "$a $a"    perl "AB AB" PCL "AB AB"  <- separated by a literal: fine
    "$a$a"     perl ABAB   PCL AB        <- SAME object, ADJACENT: ONE COPY

so the collapse needs the same BOX twice with nothing between them.  `print
$a, $a' is correct, and `$a . $a' is correct, so it is the interpolation
lowering, not the concat.

SUSPECT: `p-string-concat''s argument list is built from the interpolation
scan, and two adjacent identical pieces are being deduplicated somewhere
between `Pl::InterpScan' and the emitted `(p-string-concat $a $a)' -- read
the EMITTED form first (`./pl2cl' on the three-line reproducer), which
distinguishes a codegen collapse from a runtime one in one command.

BAR: the three rows above vs perl; whichever of corpus-diff / the sweep the
layer turns out to need; a guard row.
subject: the SAME box interpolated twice ADJACENTLY yields one copy ("$a$a")
